Audience: Readers of Black fiction, culinary fiction, and redemption-arc/found-family stories — people who want a love story that's really about ownership, sobriety, and community, not just romance.
Promise: A chef who builds his own kitchen after years of building other people's visions — and the woman whose voice opens every door in the French Quarter.

Differentiator: Semi-autobiographical, grounded New Orleans setting; food and craft are never garnish, they carry the plot; real specific stories stand in for invented drama.
Voice Notes: Polished/literary, full sentences, deliberate rhythm; short fragments used for effect not as a constant style; dry playful banter between characters, controlled narration. Never: trademarked real business names as fact, invented specific dates/venues, silently fixing continuity errors instead of flagging them.
